claim: UNHCR's 2021 operational material described hundreds of thousands of conflict-displaced people, persistent insecurity along the contact line, closures of most crossing points, and difficulties accessing pensions and social entitlements in non-government-controlled areas.
limitations: Operational/humanitarian evidence; does not by itself establish wider national political attitudes or conflict escalation.

claim: UNHCR year-end reporting for 2021 described continued integration support for IDPs, a government durable-solutions strategy, housing compensation and legal assistance, indicating stabilizing institutional responses alongside unresolved displacement.
limitations: Year-end synthesis may post-date early December snapshots; admissible only after publication timing is verified for each cutoff.

claim: World Bank commentary for Ukraine in April 2021 warned that COVID-related school closures risked learning loss and widening inequality, with less-affluent households likely to face greater disadvantages.
limitations: Some claims are extrapolated from regional evidence and framed as risks/opportunities for Ukraine, not direct measurement of all Ukrainian students.

claim: In May 2021 the World Bank approved a $200 million project to improve efficiency, quality, transparency and resilience of Ukrainian higher education, including continuity under COVID-19 conditions.
limitations: Program approval shows an institutional response and resource commitment; it does not prove implementation success by each historical cutoff.

claim: UNHCR's 2021 plan noted that COVID-related movement restrictions across the contact line separated families and deepened economic hardship while violations of the ceasefire continued.
limitations: Localized to conflict-affected communities; should not be generalized to national social cohesion.

claim: UNHCR-supported World Refugee Day activities in Ukraine explicitly emphasized integration of refugees and displaced people into local communities and reported Ukraine as home to more than 700,000 IDPs.
limitations: Event-based evidence of integration efforts; not a population-level measure of actual cohesion.
